index 98c08867..a46cb03e 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/guard-shared-tree.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/guard-shared-tree.sh
@@ -66,23 +66,42 @@ cmd_noquotes="$(printf '%s' "$cmd_noquotes" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0
 #    where the body is the program. `$cmd_nohere` therefore blanks heredoc bodies for ALL rules, and
 #    LEAVES the interpreter ones in place — a property of the shell, not a heuristic tuned to today.
 #    Quote-stripping stays `commit`-only for exactly the same reason it always was.
-cmd_nohere="$cmdn"
-_hdw0="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | grep -oE "<<-?'?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*'?" | head -1 | sed -E "s/^<<-?'?//; s/'$//")"
-if [ -n "$_hdw0" ]; then
-  # Does the command OWNING the heredoc read it as a program? Tested on the text before the `<<`,
-  # which is where the interpreter is named. If so the body is CODE and every rule keeps it raw.
-  _pre0="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?[A-Za-z_].*//")"
-  if printf '%s' "$_pre0" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])(bash|sh|zsh|python3?|node|perl|ruby|php)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
-    : # interpreter heredoc — the body is the program, so it stays visible to every rule
-  # ⚠ AND THE STRIP FAILS CLOSED, reusing the rule the rebase-guard learned the hard way: `.*` is
-  #   greedy and newlines are folded, so a terminator word appearing a SECOND time as a standalone
-  #   token lets the strip swallow real commands after the heredoc (measured 2026-08-05: a body
-  #   ending `A`, then a real `git checkout origin/main -- oxydex-dsp.js`, then a stray `A` — the
-  #   checkout was stripped and the rule passed). POSIX sed has no lazy quantifier, so strip only
-  #   when the terminator appears EXACTLY ONCE standalone; anything else keeps the full text.
-  elif [ "$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | grep -oE "(^|[[:space:]])$_hdw0([[:space:]]|$)" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]; then
-    cmd_nohere="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'?.*[[:space:]]\\1([[:space:]]|$)/ /g")"
+# ⚠ THE DECISION IS MADE PER HEREDOC, WALKING THE TEXT (residue 2026-09-23-heredoc-strip-is-decided-once-
+#   for-many). It used to be made ONCE, for the first heredoc, and applied to all of them with `sed … /g`,
+#   so a plain heredoc ahead of an interpreter one (`cat > n.md <<MD … MD` then `bash <<SH git add -A SH`)
+#   blanked the interpreter's program too and every rule went blind to it. Now each `<<WORD` is judged on
+#   the text between the previous heredoc's closer and itself — which is where its owner is named.
+cmd_nohere=""
+_hd_rest="$cmdn"
+_hd_open="<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'?"
+while [[ "$_hd_rest" =~ $_hd_open ]]; do
+  _hd_tok="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"; _hd_w="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  _hd_pre="${_hd_rest%%"$_hd_tok"*}"
+  _hd_post="${_hd_rest#*"$_hd_tok"}"
+  # ⚠ THE STRIP FAILS CLOSED, reusing the rule the rebase-guard learned the hard way: a terminator word
+  #   appearing a SECOND time as a standalone token lets a strip swallow real commands after the heredoc
+  #   (measured 2026-08-05: a body ending `A`, then a real `git checkout origin/main -- oxydex-dsp.js`,
+  #   then a stray `A` — the checkout was stripped and the rule passed). So act only when the terminator
+  #   appears EXACTLY ONCE standalone in the whole command; otherwise keep the rest of the text raw.
+  if [ "$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | grep -oE "(^|[[:space:]])$_hd_w([[:space:]]|$)" | wc -l)" -ne 1 ] \
+     || ! [[ "$_hd_post" =~ (^|[[:space:]])"$_hd_w"([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
+    break
   fi
+  _hd_end="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  _hd_body="${_hd_post%%"$_hd_end"*}"
+  _hd_after="${_hd_post#*"$_hd_end"}"
+  # Does the command OWNING this heredoc read it as a program? If so the body is CODE and every rule
+  # keeps it raw — but it is still SKIPPED PAST to its closer, so text inside a program is never
+  # mistaken for a further heredoc opener.
+  if printf '%s' "$_hd_pre" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])(bash|sh|zsh|python3?|node|perl|ruby|php)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
+    cmd_nohere="$cmd_nohere$_hd_pre$_hd_tok$_hd_body$_hd_end"
+  else
+    cmd_nohere="$cmd_nohere$_hd_pre "
+  fi
+  _hd_rest="$_hd_after"
+done
+if [ -n "$_hd_rest" ]; then
+  cmd_nohere="$cmd_nohere$_hd_rest"
 fi

A same-count file would silently reuse stale vectors. A correct fix therefore needs a cache-invalidation policy (per-file versioning vs wholesale re-embed of the 718 MB cache, then reloading any index built from it). That is an owner design decision, and verifying it needs the local embedder and the corpus cache, which this sandbox lacks, so I made no change and created no branch.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+# Copyright 2026 Michal Planicka
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+#
+# hooks-drain-stdin.test.sh — every early exit that sits ABOVE a hook's stdin read must
+# still drain stdin (residue 2026-10-12-seven-hooks-exit-before-draining-stdin-and-their-
+# tests-cannot-see-it; the trim hook's own fix is #3493).
+#
+# The harness writes the tool-call JSON into the hook's stdin. A hook that exits first
+# leaves that writer on a closed pipe, and once the payload does not fit the 64 KB pipe
+# buffer the writer dies on SIGPIPE (141). Each hook's own self-test cannot see that: it
+# reads "exit code is not 2" as ALLOW, so a writer's 141 scores as the pass a hatch
+# release wants. This file asks the two questions separately:
+#   · writer_rc — the WRITER's fate, through a pipe on purpose, repeated (it is a race);
+#   · decided   — the HOOK's own exit code, fed by redirect so no writer is involved.
+# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
+set -uo pipefail
+D="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+fail=0
+TMP="$(mktemp -d)"

+writer_rc() { # writer_rc <hook-path> <trials> [hook-args…] — worst exit code of the process WRITING to the hook
+  local h="$1" n="$2" i rc worst=0; shift 2
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do

+    rc="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
+    [ "$rc" != 0 ] && worst="$rc"
+  done

+decided() { # decided <hook-path> [hook-args…] — the hook's own exit code, no pipe
+  local h="$1"; shift

+  else printf '  FAIL  %-62s got %s, want %s (141 = SIGPIPE: the hook never read stdin)\n' "$3" "$2" "$1"; fail=$((fail+1)); fi

+leg 0   "$(writer_rc "$TMP/drain.sh" 1)"   '…and one that drains first does not'
+
+echo "── each escape hatch drains stdin, and still releases ────────────────────"

+  guard-format:CLAUDE_ALLOW_UNFORMATTED \
+  guard-ruff:CLAUDE_ALLOW_UNFORMATTED \
+  guard-trailer:CLAUDE_ALLOW_NO_TRAILER \
+  guard-stale-brief:CLAUDE_ALLOW_STALE_BRIEF \
+  guard-memory-stale:CLAUDE_ALLOW_STALE_MEMORY \
+  guard-shared-tree:CLAUDE_ALLOW_BLANKET_GIT; do
+  h="${pair%%:*}"; v="${pair#*:}"

+  leg 0 "$(export "$v=1"; decided "$D/$h.sh" pre)"     "$h: …and the hatch still releases"
+done
+
+echo "── guard-doc-search: the absent-tool exits drain too ─────────────────────"
+# A PATH holding cat and git but no jq, then one holding cat and jq but no git.
+mkdir -p "$TMP/nojq" "$TMP/nogit"
+ln -s "$(command -v cat)" "$TMP/nojq/cat";  ln -s "$(command -v git)" "$TMP/nojq/git"
+ln -s "$(command -v cat)" "$TMP/nogit/cat"; ln -s "$(command -v jq)"  "$TMP/nogit/jq"
+BASH_BIN="$(command -v bash)"
+nopath_rc() { # nopath_rc <path-dir> — writer rc with the hook running under a reduced PATH
+  local i rc worst=0
+  for ((i = 0; i < 5; i++)); do
+    cat "$TMP/big.json" | env -u CLAUDE_ALLOW_NO_DOC_SEARCH PATH="$1" "$BASH_BIN" "$D/guard-doc-search.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
+    rc="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
+    [ "$rc" != 0 ] && worst="$rc"
+  done
+  printf '%s' "$worst"
+}
+leg 0 "$(nopath_rc "$TMP/nojq")"  'guard-doc-search: no jq on PATH drains, 5 writers live'
+leg 0 "$(nopath_rc "$TMP/nogit")" 'guard-doc-search: no git on PATH drains, 5 writers live'

+# guard-memory-stale exits before reading on a HOME with no memory directory, a measured
+# 6.6 ms-per-call trade documented in the hook. Draining there spends that decision, which
+# is the owner's call, so the residue row stays open for this one path.

diff --git a/capture-host/tests/test_runtime_licences.py b/capture-host/tests/test_runtime_licences.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..28fc3911
--- /dev/null
+++ b/capture-host/tests/test_runtime_licences.py
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+# Copyright 2026 Michal Planicka
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Every runtime library in requirements.txt has a licence row in THIRD-PARTY.md.
+
+Residue 2026-10-12-four-capture-host-runtime-libraries-are-named-in-no-licence-doc: running the
+capture-host installs bleak, PyYAML, aiohttp and cryptography, and the licence doc named none of them.
+Its capture-host section covered device protocols only. This test reads `requirements.txt` and the
+capture-host runtime table in `THIRD-PARTY.md`, not a copy of either, so the next runtime dependency
+that is added without a licence row reds here.
+"""
+
+import pathlib
+import re
+
+HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+REQ = HERE / "requirements.txt"
+THIRD_PARTY = HERE.parent / "THIRD-PARTY.md"
+HEADING = "### Capture-host runtime libraries"
+
+_PKG = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)")
+
+
+def _norm(name: str) -> str:
+    """PEP 503 normalisation, so `PyYAML` / `pyyaml` / `py_yaml` compare equal."""
+    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()
+
+
+def runtime_packages(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    out: set[str] = set()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        m = _PKG.match(line.strip())
+        if m:
+            out.add(_norm(m.group(1)))
+    return out
+
+
+def licence_rows(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """`{package: licence cell}` from the table under HEADING, up to the next heading or rule.
+
+    A row names its package as the first `code span` in column one: `| **bleak** (`bleak`) | … |`.
+    An absent heading yields `{}`, so the comparison below reds instead of passing vacuously."""
+    rows: dict[str, str] = {}
+    _, found, rest = text.partition(HEADING + "\n")
+    if not found:
+        return rows
+    for line in rest.splitlines():
+        if line.startswith("#") or line.strip() == "---":
+            break
+        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
+        name = re.search(r"`([^`]+)`", cells[0]) if line.startswith("|") and len(cells) >= 3 else None
+        if name:
+            rows[_norm(name.group(1))] = cells[2]
+    return rows
+
+
+def test_every_runtime_library_has_a_licence_row_in_third_party():
+    declared = runtime_packages(REQ.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    # A parser that matched nothing would pass vacuously — pin the population it must have seen.
+    assert {"bleak", "pyyaml", "aiohttp", "cryptography"} <= declared, declared
+    rows = licence_rows(THIRD_PARTY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    missing = declared - set(rows)
+    assert not missing, f"requirements.txt declares these but THIRD-PARTY.md gives no licence row: {sorted(missing)}"
+    unread = sorted(p for p in declared if not rows[p])
+    assert not unread, f"these rows carry no licence: {unread}"
+
+
+# ── the parsers must be able to fail ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def test_the_parser_reads_past_comments_and_version_specifiers():
+    text = "# header\n\nbleak>=0.22   # BLE\nPyYAML>=6.0.3\n#   - pipx install muselsl\n"
+    assert runtime_packages(text) == {"bleak", "pyyaml"}
+
+
+def test_a_missing_row_and_a_missing_heading_are_both_reported():
+    doc = (
+        f"{HEADING}\n\n| library | version | licence | use |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
+        "| **bleak** (`bleak`) | 3.0.2 | MIT | BLE |\n\n---\n| **aiohttp** (`aiohttp`) | 3 | MIT | x |\n"
+    )
+    assert licence_rows(doc) == {"bleak": "MIT"}, "a row after the section's rule is not in the section"
+    assert {"bleak", "aiohttp"} - set(licence_rows(doc)) == {"aiohttp"}
+    assert licence_rows("| **bleak** (`bleak`) | 3.0.2 | MIT | BLE |\n") == {}

index 98c08867..11dd5d4b 100755
--- a/.claude/hooks/guard-shared-tree.sh
+++ b/.claude/hooks/guard-shared-tree.sh
@@ -67,22 +67,46 @@ cmd_noquotes="$(printf '%s' "$cmd_noquotes" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0

 #    Quote-stripping stays `commit`-only for exactly the same reason it always was.
 cmd_nohere="$cmdn"
-_hdw0="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | grep -oE "<<-?'?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*'?" | head -1 | sed -E "s/^<<-?'?//; s/'$//")"
-if [ -n "$_hdw0" ]; then
-  # Does the command OWNING the heredoc read it as a program? Tested on the text before the `<<`,
-  # which is where the interpreter is named. If so the body is CODE and every rule keeps it raw.
-  _pre0="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?[A-Za-z_].*//")"
-  if printf '%s' "$_pre0" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])(bash|sh|zsh|python3?|node|perl|ruby|php)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
-    : # interpreter heredoc — the body is the program, so it stays visible to every rule
-  # ⚠ AND THE STRIP FAILS CLOSED, reusing the rule the rebase-guard learned the hard way: `.*` is
-  #   greedy and newlines are folded, so a terminator word appearing a SECOND time as a standalone
-  #   token lets the strip swallow real commands after the heredoc (measured 2026-08-05: a body
-  #   ending `A`, then a real `git checkout origin/main -- oxydex-dsp.js`, then a stray `A` — the
-  #   checkout was stripped and the rule passed). POSIX sed has no lazy quantifier, so strip only
-  #   when the terminator appears EXACTLY ONCE standalone; anything else keeps the full text.
-  elif [ "$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | grep -oE "(^|[[:space:]])$_hdw0([[:space:]]|$)" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]; then
-    cmd_nohere="$(printf '%s' "$cmdn" | sed -E "s/<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'?.*[[:space:]]\\1([[:space:]]|$)/ /g")"
-  fi
+# ── THE DECISION IS MADE PER HEREDOC, WHILE WALKING THE TEXT (residue
+#    2026-09-23-heredoc-strip-is-decided-once-for-many). The first form decided interpreter-vs-data
+#    ONCE, for the FIRST heredoc, then stripped with `sed … /g`. So a plain heredoc ahead of an
+#    interpreter heredoc blanked the interpreter's body too, and `git add -A` in that body passed.
+#    Each opener now gets its own test, on the text between the previous terminator and its `<<`.
+#    Offsets come from `%%` and `${#…}`, never from `#*…`, which is quadratic on a long command.
+if [[ "$cmdn" == *"<<"* ]]; then
+  _hdre="<<-?'?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'?"
+  _hdrest="$cmdn"; _hdout=""
+  while [[ "$_hdrest" =~ $_hdre ]]; do
+    _hdop="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"; _hdw0="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+    _pre0="${_hdrest%%"$_hdop"*}"
+    _post0="${_hdrest:$(( ${#_pre0} + ${#_hdop} ))}"
+    # ⚠ AND THE WALK FAILS CLOSED, reusing the rule the rebase-guard learned the hard way: newlines
+    #   are folded, so a terminator word appearing a SECOND time as a standalone token cannot be told
+    #   from the closer, and a wrong guess swallows real commands after the heredoc (measured
+    #   2026-08-05: a body ending `A`, then a real `git checkout origin/main -- oxydex-dsp.js`, then a
+    #   stray `A` — the checkout was stripped and the rule passed). So the walk goes on only when the
+    #   terminator appears EXACTLY ONCE standalone after the opener; else the rest stays raw. The
+    #   count splits on whitespace, because `grep -o` shares no space between matches and reads
+    #   `A A` as one.
+    [ "$(printf '%s' "$_post0" | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | grep -cxF -- "$_hdw0")" -eq 1 ] || break
+    # One trailing space gives the terminator a right edge at the end of the text too, so the first
+    # literal occurrence of `$_hdterm` IS the standalone one (a bare ` A` is also the head of ` AB`).
+    _hdx="$_post0 "
+    [[ "$_hdx" =~ (^|[[:space:]])$_hdw0[[:space:]] ]] || break
+    _hdterm="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+    _hdbody="${_hdx%%"$_hdterm"*}"
+    _hdafter="${_post0:$(( ${#_hdbody} + ${#_hdterm} ))}"
+    # Does the command OWNING the heredoc read it as a program? Tested on the text between the
+    # previous terminator and this `<<`, which is where the interpreter is named. If so the body is
+    # CODE and every rule keeps it raw; otherwise the body is data and is blanked.
+    if printf '%s' "$_pre0" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])(bash|sh|zsh|python3?|node|perl|ruby|php)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
+      _hdout+="$_pre0$_hdop$_hdbody$_hdterm"
+    else
+      _hdout+="$_pre0 "
+    fi
+    _hdrest="$_hdafter"
+  done
+  cmd_nohere="$_hdout$_hdrest"
 fi

+# ── NIGHT ABSENT: an EXPECTED device with no primary file is its own class ──────────────────────────
+# Residue `2026-09-23-loss-audit-cannot-attribute-a-night-with-no-file`. `lost_min` counts gaps INSIDE a
+# recorded span, so a device with no span added nothing to the ledger, and the 2026-09-18 night (H10

+# config's own word: a device is expected unless it is `optional: true` (config.example.yaml,
+# KNOWN-BUT-NOT-EXPECTED), and a model with no known primary stream cannot be judged absent.

+def _absent_night_devices():
+    return DEV + [
+        {"name": "Wellue O2Ring-S", "model": "O2Ring-S"},
+        {"name": "Polar Sense 0C301E3F", "model": "VeritySense"},
+        {"name": "Backup ring", "model": "O2Ring-S", "optional": True},
+        {"name": "COOSPO 808S", "model": "HRM808S"},
+    ]
+

+    """The 2026-09-18 shape: one device recorded and lost nothing, two expected devices left no file. The
+    worn fraction over the present device is 0.0, which is the headline met — and a stated
+    sub-population (the expected devices) missed, which is SHORTFALL by the verdict contract, never
+    PASS. The class is keyed on the config, not inferred from an absence of rows: the optional backup
+    with no file and the model with no primary stream are NOT night-absent."""
+    d = _night(tmp_path, holes=())
+    a = loss_audit.audit_night(d, _absent_night_devices(), journal=lambda *a: [])
+    assert a["devices"]["Polar H10 0284"]["lost_min"] == 0.0
+    assert a["devices"]["Polar H10 0284"]["worn_evidence"] is True
+    assert a["devices"]["Wellue O2Ring-S"]["night_absent"] is True
+    assert a["devices"]["Polar Sense 0C301E3F"]["night_absent"] is True
+    assert a["devices"]["Backup ring"]["night_absent"] is False, "an optional backup is not expected"
+    assert "night_absent" not in a["devices"]["COOSPO 808S"], "no primary stream known ⇒ not judged"

+    assert o["result"]["night_absent"] == ["Polar Sense 0C301E3F", "Wellue O2Ring-S"]
+    assert o["result"]["worn_but_not_recorded_fraction"] == 0.0
+    assert o["population"] == {"checked": 1, "eligible": 5, "excluded": 4}
+    assert o["reason"] == (

+    optional backup with no file, still PASS with `night_absent: []`."""

+    assert nr["reason"] == (
+        "no configured device left a primary stream this night; "
+        "night absent: Polar H10 0284, Polar Sense 0C301E3F, Wellue O2Ring-S"
+    )

+    na = loss_audit.night_verdict(
+        {"devices": {**_audit({"Polar H10": (100.0, 0.0, False)})["devices"], "Ring": absent}, "journal": "read"},

+            clean, DEV + [{"name": "Backup ring", "model": "O2Ring-S", "optional": True}], journal=lambda *a: []

diff --git a/capture-host/deploy/tepna-capture.service b/capture-host/deploy/tepna-capture.service
index 4f9b433a..6c7a336d 100644
--- a/capture-host/deploy/tepna-capture.service
+++ b/capture-host/deploy/tepna-capture.service
@@ -6,7 +6,7 @@ Description=Tepna capture daemon (BLE -> vendor-layout files)
 # with 97 warnings). A "clean journal" claim must publish its DENOMINATOR ("97 of 10,836"), never a bare
 # "no warnings"; re-run the same query with no unit filter first, to see whether the journal has any lines.
 # Needs the Bluetooth stack and a synced clock (arrival stamps depend on the clock).
-After=bluetooth.target network-online.target time-sync.target
+After=bluetooth.target network-online.target time-sync.target avahi-daemon.service
 Wants=bluetooth.target network-online.target
 # Capture is unattended overnight — never rate-limit restarts (keep retrying across transient BLE drops).
 # StartLimitIntervalSec lives in [Unit], not [Service], since systemd v230 — it was silently IGNORED in
@@ -44,6 +44,25 @@ AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_ADMIN
 
 Group=vigil
 WorkingDirectory=/opt/tepna/capture-host
+# ⚠️ AVAHI CAN RENAME THIS BOX AND KEEP THE NEW NAME. On 2026-09-23 a boot 26 min after the previous one logged
+# `Host name conflict, retrying with vigil-2` -> `Host name is vigil-2.local` with nothing else on the LAN
+# holding `vigil.local`. avahi kept `vigil-2.local` for four hours; `http://vigil.local/monitor` did not
+# resolve while localhost/monitor served 200, and no journal line said so. `systemctl restart avahi-daemon`
+# reclaimed the name (RESIDUE 2026-09-23-avahi-renames-the-box-after-a-quick-reboot; 2 renames in 13 boot
+# transitions, Wren 2026-10-12). So at every start: ask avahi which name it advertises (D-Bus GetHostName)
+# and compare it with `hostname` cut at the first dot, as avahi cuts it. A mismatch logs a <4> WARNING in
+# THIS unit's journal (`journalctl -u tepna-capture -p warning`) and restarts avahi without waiting for it.
+# No reply is UNKNOWN, logged at <5>, and restarts nothing (ABSENCE IS NULL: no reply is not a rename).
+# `+` runs the check as root, which a restart needs, and the code is INLINE on purpose: root installs this
+# file into /etc from origin/main, so no file `vigil` can write runs as root (see tepna-sysfiles.sh).
+# `-` keeps a failed check from blocking capture. `$$` and `%%` are systemd's escapes for `$` and `%`.
+# Limit: a conflict that avahi detects after this start goes unseen until the next capture start.
+ExecStartPre=-+/bin/sh -c 'h=$$(hostname); h=$${h%%%%.*}; \
+  set -- $$(busctl --timeout=5 call org.freedesktop.Avahi / org.freedesktop.Avahi.Server GetHostName 2>/dev/null); \
+  if [ "$$1" != s ] || [ -z "$$2" ]; then echo "<5>avahi host name unknown: no GetHostName reply, nothing restarted"; exit 0; fi; \
+  n=$${2#?}; n=$${n%%?}; [ "$$n" = "$$h" ] && exit 0; \
+  echo "<4>avahi advertises $$n.local, not $$h.local: restarting avahi-daemon to reclaim the name"; \
+  systemctl --no-block restart avahi-daemon.service'
 # Use the venv's python (see README install).
 ExecStart=/opt/tepna/capture-host/.venv/bin/python capture.py --config /opt/tepna/capture-host/config.yaml
 Restart=always

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+# tepna-capture — tests/test_capture_unit_avahi_name.py
+# Copyright 2026 Michal Planicka
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""The capture unit reclaims the mDNS name when avahi renamed the box, and says so in its journal.
+
+RESIDUE `2026-09-23-avahi-renames-the-box-after-a-quick-reboot`: the 18:42 boot on 2026-09-23 logged
+`Host name conflict, retrying with vigil-2` -> `Host name is vigil-2.local`, 26 min after the previous
+boot. Nothing else on the LAN held the name. avahi kept `vigil-2.local` for four hours, so
+`http://vigil.local/monitor` did not resolve while the monitor served 200 on localhost. No line in any
+journal the fleet reads said so. `sudo systemctl restart avahi-daemon` at 22:42 reclaimed `vigil.local`.
+Wren's 2026-10-12 box survey found two such renames in 13 boot transitions, each held until a restart.
+
+The check lives IN the unit file, as an inline `+` (root) ExecStartPre. Root installs that file into
+/etc from origin/main, so no file that `vigil` can write runs as root. tepna-sysfiles.sh states that
+trust boundary.
+
+These tests drive the REAL command text from the unit, after the same continuation, specifier (`%%`) and
+dollar (`$$`) unescaping that systemd applies, with `hostname`, `busctl` and `systemctl` stubbed.
+"""
+
+import os
+import re
+import shlex
+import subprocess
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+UNIT = os.path.join(HERE, "deploy", "tepna-capture.service")
+
+
+def _unit():
+    with open(UNIT, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        # systemd joins a line that ends in a backslash with the next one, and the backslash becomes a space.
+        return f.read().replace("\\\n", " ")
+
+
+def _avahi_pre():
+    """(prefix, argv) of the one ExecStartPre that names avahi, or (None, None)."""
+    hits = [ln for ln in _unit().splitlines() if ln.startswith("ExecStartPre=") and "avahi" in ln.lower()]
+    if len(hits) != 1:
+        return None, None
+    cmd = hits[0][len("ExecStartPre=") :]
+    m = re.match(r"^([-+@:!]*)(.*)$", cmd)
+    prefix, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2)
+    rest = rest.replace("%%", "%").replace("$$", "$")
+    return prefix, shlex.split(rest)
+
+
+def _run(tmp_path, busctl_out, busctl_rc=0, host="vigil"):
+    prefix, argv = _avahi_pre()
+    assert argv is not None, "tepna-capture.service has no ExecStartPre that checks the avahi host name"
+    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
+    bin_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    log = tmp_path / "calls.log"
+    log.write_text("")
+    stubs = {
+        "hostname": f"#!/bin/sh\necho {host}\n",
+        "busctl": f"#!/bin/sh\necho \"busctl $*\" >> \"{log}\"\nprintf '%s\\n' '{busctl_out}'\nexit {busctl_rc}\n",
+        "systemctl": f'#!/bin/sh\necho "systemctl $*" >> "{log}"\nexit 0\n',
+    }
+    for name, body in stubs.items():
+        p = bin_dir / name
+        p.write_text(body)
+        p.chmod(0o755)
+    env = {**os.environ, "PATH": f"{bin_dir}:{os.environ['PATH']}"}
+    r = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=30)
+    return r, log.read_text()
+
+
+def test_the_check_runs_as_root_and_never_blocks_capture():
+    prefix, argv = _avahi_pre()
+    assert argv is not None, "tepna-capture.service has no ExecStartPre that checks the avahi host name"
+    assert "+" in prefix, "restarting avahi needs root, and the unit runs as User=vigil"
+    assert "-" in prefix, "a failed name check must never keep capture from starting"
+    assert re.search(r"^After=.*\bavahi-daemon\.service\b", _unit(), re.M)
+
+
+def test_a_renamed_box_is_reported_at_warning_and_avahi_is_restarted(tmp_path):
+    r, calls = _run(tmp_path, 's "vigil-2"')
+    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
+    assert "GetHostName" in calls
+    assert "systemctl --no-block restart avahi-daemon.service" in calls
+    warn = [ln for ln in r.stdout.splitlines() if ln.startswith("<4>")]
+    assert len(warn) == 1 and "vigil-2.local" in warn[0] and "vigil.local" in warn[0], r.stdout
+
+
+def test_the_hostname_name_is_left_alone(tmp_path):
+    r, calls = _run(tmp_path, 's "vigil"')
+    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
+    assert "GetHostName" in calls
+    assert "systemctl" not in calls
+    assert "<4>" not in r.stdout
+
+
+def test_an_unread_name_is_unknown_not_a_mismatch(tmp_path):
+    """ABSENCE IS NULL: avahi down or no reply is not evidence of a rename, so nothing is restarted."""
+    r, calls = _run(tmp_path, "", busctl_rc=1)
+    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
+    assert "systemctl" not in calls
+    assert "<4>" not in r.stdout
+    assert any(ln.startswith("<5>") and "unknown" in ln for ln in r.stdout.splitlines()), r.stdout
+
+
+def test_a_dotted_hostname_is_cut_at_the_first_dot_as_avahi_cuts_it(tmp_path):
+    r, calls = _run(tmp_path, 's "vigil"', host="vigil.lan")
+    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
+    assert "systemctl" not in calls
+    assert "<4>" not in r.stdout

--- a/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py
+++ b/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py
@@ -6668,3 +6668,37 @@ def test_the_RECORDED_and_the_RECOVERED_offset_AGREE_on_one_night_in_one_zone(tm
     finally:
         monkeypatch.delenv("TZ", raising=False)
         time.tzset()
+

+def test_the_daemon_restart_count_reads_the_SAME_walk_the_summary_reports(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """mutant `x_summarize__mutmut_17`: `daemon_starts(night_dir, None, …)` in place of `scanned` walks the
+    night a SECOND time. On a live night the folder moves between the two walks, so `daemon.inside_capture`
+    is judged against files that `files` / `total_rows` never counted: one summary, two snapshots.
+
+    The spy lets the first walk of this folder return, then a new connection opens a file whose span covers
+    the recorded restart. Judged against the walk the summary reports, the restart fell OUTSIDE capture."""
+    night = str(tmp_path / "2026-09-24")
+    os.makedirs(night)
+    t0 = _stamp_epoch("20260924210000")
+    seam = t0 + 1200  # the daemon restarts 10 min after the only snapshotted file closed
+    _abs_cap(night, t0, 600, t0 + 600)
+    _starts(night, seam)
+    real_scan = nightqc.scan_night
+    walks = []
+
+    def _scan_then_a_device_opens(d):
+        got = real_scan(d)
+        if d == night:
+            walks.append(d)
+            if len(walks) == 1:  # a connection that opens AFTER the walk and spans the restart
+                _abs_cap(night, t0 + 900, 600, t0 + 1500)
+        return got
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(nightqc, "scan_night", _scan_then_a_device_opens)
+    s = nightqc.summarize(night, _DEV_HR, writer_offset=nightqc.declared_offset(_X))
+    assert s["files"] == 1, "the CONTROL: the summary reports the first walk — the HR file alone"
+    assert s["daemon"]["starts"] == 1 and s["daemon"]["stamps"] == [seam + _X], s["daemon"]
+    assert s["daemon"]["inside_capture"] == 0, (
+        f"the restart is judged against a walk the summary does not report: {s['daemon']!r}"
+    )
+    assert walks == [night], f"the night is walked once, not {len(walks)} times"

@@ -6668,3 +6668,31 @@ def test_the_RECORDED_and_the_RECOVERED_offset_AGREE_on_one_night_in_one_zone(tm

+def test_summarize_hands_daemon_starts_the_night_it_ALREADY_walked(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """`summarize` walks the night once and hands that scan to `daemon_starts`, whose docstring makes it
+    the caller's job: "callers that already have it pass it rather than walking the night twice".
+
+    Kills `nightqc.x_summarize__mutmut_20` (#3188), the dropped `scanned` argument. That mutant changes no
+    returned field on a folder that holds still, because `daemon_starts` then re-runs `scan_night` on the

+    the rows of every file, so the mutant re-reads the whole growing night on every QC poll, and on a live
+    night the restart count comes from a different snapshot than the sessions it is reported beside. So the

+    real_scan = nightqc.scan_night
+    walks = []
+

+        walks.append(os.path.abspath(d))
+        return real_scan(d)

+    s = _summarize_floating(night, devs)
+    assert s["daemon"]["starts"] == 2, ("the CONTROL: the sidecar's two recorded starts must be read", s["daemon"])
+    assert walks.count(os.path.abspath(night)) == 1, (

rows.patch_text:
diff --git a/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py b/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py
index 6022b20e..7f209533 100644
--- a/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py
+++ b/capture-host/tests/test_nightqc.py
@@ -6668,3 +6668,34 @@ def test_the_RECORDED_and_the_RECOVERED_offset_AGREE_on_one_night_in_one_zone(tm
     finally:
         monkeypatch.delenv("TZ", raising=False)
         time.tzset()
+
+
+def test_the_POOLED_previous_folder_is_walked_ONCE_its_daemon_starts_reuses_the_scan(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """mutant 103: `daemon_starts(prev, offset_sec=…)` without `prev_data` makes it re-run `scan_night`
+    on the folder `summarize` has just scanned. The summary is identical — `stamps` and `starts` come
+    from the sidecar alone — so only the walk count can show it. `daemon_starts`'s contract says
+    "callers that already have it pass it rather than walking the night twice", and `scan_night` reads
+    every file end to end, so the second walk is the whole pooled day read again."""
+    d23 = str(tmp_path / "2026-09-23")
+    d24 = str(tmp_path / "2026-09-24")
+    os.makedirs(d23)
+    os.makedirs(d24)
+    a = _stamp_epoch("20260923220000")
+    seam = a + 3600
+    _abs_cap(d23, a, 3600, seam)
+    _abs_cap(d23, seam, 3000, seam + 3000)
+    _starts(d23, seam)  # the sidecar must exist, or `daemon_starts` returns before it reads `files`
+    c = _stamp_epoch("20260924001000")  # 00:10, inside the near-midnight pool window
+    _abs_cap(d24, c, 3000, c + 3000)
+    walks = []
+    real_scan = nightqc.scan_night
+
+    def counting_scan(night_dir):
+        walks.append(os.path.basename(night_dir))
+        return real_scan(night_dir)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(nightqc, "scan_night", counting_scan)
+    s = nightqc.summarize(d24, _DEV_HR, writer_offset=nightqc.declared_offset(_X))
+    assert len(s["searched_dirs"]) == 2, ("the CONTROL: the previous folder is pooled", s["searched_dirs"])
+    assert s["daemon"]["stamps"] == [seam + _X], ("the CONTROL: its seam is read", s["daemon"])
+    assert walks.count("2026-09-23") == 1, ("the pooled folder was walked more than once", walks)

The mutant is EQUIVALENT: `after` is an in-order subset of `merge_sessions` output, which comes back with strictly increasing starts and disjoint intervals with s[0] <= s[1] (file_interval returns end=max(start,mtime), or start plus a span that file_span_sec/file_host_span_sec only return when it is above 0; the seam clamp keeps each end at or before the next start). So ends never decrease, and `min` by s[1] returns the same first element as `min` by s[0], even on a tie. My probe /mnt/session/outputs/probe_mutmut_234.py checked 87,299 `after` sets from real merge_sessions output (offsets 0, ±h and None, with daemon starts, touching sessions, stampless files and span_sec) and found 0 where the two keys pick a different session. Any test that kills the mutant would have to monkeypatch merge_sessions to break its own documented ORDERED AND DISJOINT contract, so I added no test and did not change nightqc.py.

@@ -525,3 +525,26 @@ def test_default_clock_is_real_monotonic_and_wall_matches_the_link_axis():
     pw = P.RingPower(ADDR)

+# ── §24 "manual pull during cooldown → runs" with "illegal_skipped == 0 over the night" ─────────────
+def test_an_attempt_started_inside_a_cooldown_leaves_through_radio_idle_and_skips_no_edge():
+    """The operator's pull is ungated (§3.2), so it can start inside a cooldown. COOLDOWN → CONNECTING is
+    illegal by design (§2), and the engine skipped the attempt's edges: it counted illegal transitions and
+    showed the radio OFF for a pull that held it. The attempt now leaves through RADIO_IDLE. The deadline
+    stays: an operator's pull overrides the cooldown, it does not end it."""
+    pw, _ = _pw()
+    _detected(pw)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        pw.cache.backoff_until = None
+        _fail(pw, 100.0)
+    assert pw.state is S.COOLDOWN
+    until = pw.cache.cooldown_until
+    pw.drain()
+    pw.attempt_started("manual", 200.0)
+    assert pw.state is S.CONNECTING and pw.state in P.RADIO_ON
+    pw.attempt_finished(230.0, ok=False, failure=F.TIMEOUT)
+    assert pw.counters.illegal_skipped == 0
+    assert [t.new for t in pw.drain()] == [S.RADIO_IDLE, S.CONNECTING, S.HARVESTING, S.DISCONNECTING, S.COOLDOWN]
+    assert pw.counters.cooldowns == 2 and pw.cache.cooldown_until == pytest.approx(230.0 + P.STRIKE_COOLDOWN_S)
+    assert until is not None and not pw.attempt_allowed(231.0).allowed

+def test_a_manual_pull_during_a_cooldown_runs_and_the_power_axis_records_it(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """§24 — "manual pull during cooldown → runs" and "`illegal_skipped == 0` over the night", through the
+    real monitor path (`pull_oxyii_session` with its default `manual` trigger). The pull ran on the base
+    code too, but the engine skipped CONNECTING and DISCONNECTING as illegal edges out of COOLDOWN."""
+    import pull_session
+
+    _quiet_pull_env(monkeypatch)
+    f = tmp_path / "Wellue_O2Ring-S_S1_20260905_STORED.dat"
+    f.write_bytes(b"x" * 7)
+
+    async def fake_pull(address, out_dir, **kw):
+        return [str(f)]
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(pull_session, "pull", fake_pull)

+    pw.note_cooldown(1e12, "restart storm hold")
+    pw.drain()
+    r = _run(capture.pull_oxyii_session(_ring(), str(tmp_path)))
+    assert r["ok"] is True and r["new_files"] == [f.name], "the operator's pull runs inside a cooldown"
+    assert pw.counters.illegal_skipped == 0
+    S = oxy_power.PowerState
+    walked = [t.new for t in pw.drain()]
+    assert walked == [S.RADIO_IDLE, S.CONNECTING, S.HARVESTING, S.DISCONNECTING, S.RADIO_IDLE]
+    assert capture.STATUS["power"]["Ring"]["last_attempt"]["trigger"] == "manual"
+    assert pw.cache.cooldown_until == 1e12, "the override does not end the cooldown"
+    assert not pw.attempt_allowed(capture._time.monotonic()).allowed

PATCH: oxyCoverage (oxydex-dsp.js) builds recording.coverage.segments from row.t, which is the compat Date. JSON then writes startMs as an ISO "…Z" string, where ECGDex, PpgDex and GlucoDex goldens carry a number. That breaks Clock Contract §1 (never store a Date or string as truth) and puts the wrong unit on the export boundary. integrator-dsp recSegments (isFinite(startMs)) then drops every OxyDex segment: end to end on uploads/synthetic_oxydex_o2ring_gap.csv, recSegments(wire) returned null instead of 2 segments, and in memory it returned string-concatenated edges. So gap-aware overlap and the apnea denominator silently fall back to the 120 min envelope where 5398 s was recorded. The one-line fix coerces the edge to ms. Regression gate: the same group is red on the base and green with the fix, --group=oxydex has 2249 passing assertions and 12 skips, and --group=coverage has 651 passing. The OxyDex.html rebuild, npm run check and a changeset are still owed. No OxyDex golden carries coverage, so no fixture moves. FINDING: oxyBuildSpo2Series sizes the grid with floor() but places rows with round(). Input: rows [{tMs:t0,spo2:95}] plus 10 rows at t0+i*1000+600 ms. Result: n=11, but only 10 cells are non-null, the last row is dropped (k=11>=n), and index 1 is an empty cell although a sample existed at +1.6 s. Assertion to replay (I ran this in a scratch realm, not in the suite): 'every row lands on the 1 Hz grid' got 10 · want 11. FINDING: _o2BinStartMs uses file.lastModified as the full start instant, and the sibling _o2DateAnchorMs uses only its date. Input: _o2BinStartMs('ring.dat',{lastModified:Date.UTC(2026,5,11,9,30)}) under TZ=UTC gives 2026-06-11T09:30:00Z, while _o2DateAnchorMs gives 00:00. The undated .dat night is therefore stamped from the download time of day. Assertion to replay (I ran this in a scratch realm, not in the suite): 'start time of day comes from the data, not the file mtime' got 09:30 · want null or 00:00. Owner decision needed. Cited, not new: rows counted as seconds (n/3600, computeCTprecise) → RESIDUE 2026-09-29-oxydex-counts-rows-as-seconds; NADIR_RAMP_MAX_SEC used as an index count → 2026-10-07-nadir-ramp-max-sec-is-a-duration-applied-as-an-index-count; parseTimeStr returns 0 → 2026-10-06-parsetimestr-zero-on-unparseable; the unanchored /(\d{14})/ in _o2BinStartMs → 2026-10-12-filename-stamp-consumers-split-twelve-convert-four-identify.
